reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that hunger drives a structured, goal-oriented exploration process. As physiological demand increases, so does the organism’s readiness to engage in exploratory behaviors that are functionally linked to reward acquisition. This is not random but rather a means-end-readiness—whereby exploratory actions are evaluated based on their likelihood of yielding food. The transition from naive to maze-wise behavior reflects a learned optimization of these actions, where past success shapes future choices. In GSI terms, this manifests as a Bayesian update over reward probabilities, while in GSE, it translates into a reinforcement learning framework where action values are updated through trial-and-error. The failure mode occurs when the organism becomes trapped in suboptimal exploration strategies due to insufficient feedback or environmental rigidity.
